subject: Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain was a paladin of Bahamut who died three years ago in Daggerford while breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation. His severed bronze forearm is mounted on a stone pillar as a monument, bearing a Stroudite inscription and signed by Milo Goodbarrel of the Order of the Gauntlet.
source_quote: The primary inscription read: 'Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years. Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.'

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is the head of a publisher and a member of the Order of the Gauntlet who personally witnessed and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, signing it with the phrase 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.'
source_quote: The smaller inscription on the back read: 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.' Signed by Milo Goodbarrel.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, possibly containing Stroudite members, and commissioned the bronze forearm statue despite its conflicting religious inscriptions.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet endorsed the monument to Tarvis Ulain, with Milo Goodbarrel signing off on its recording, and now sells pewter hand casts as donations to support their cause.
source_quote: He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford when Tarvis Ulain intervened and died stopping them, marking him as a martyr in the region's post-war religious landscape.
source_quote: Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: monument unveiling
fact: A bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain was unveiled in Daggerford's market square, bearing a Stroudite inscription and a Gauntlet-approved record, creating theological tension between Bahamutian and Stroudite factions.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar... The secondary inscription... *The move is yours.*

subject: pewter hand cast sales
fact: A village priest began selling miniature pewter reproductions of Tarvis Ulain's severed hand as donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, sparking irony and unease among the party due to their size and the monument's symbolism.
source_quote: He was carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: Underdark corruption
fact: A pervasive, non-magical corruption from the Underdark is bleeding upward, disrupting perception and communication among surface dwellers, manifesting as auditory hallucinations and compulsive drawing in children like Elin.
source_quote: Something from below was bleeding up, that it was affecting how people processed what reached them.

subject: Elin
fact: Elin, a 7-year-old girl from Maerith, has been silent for six days and compulsively draws a six-pointed star on every flat surface, while speaking in her sleep with the phrase 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface... She says it is only the shape that holds... 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum, a cleric of Bahamut, is deeply attuned to spiritual and metaphysical disturbances, documenting the connection between Elin's condition and Daz's headaches as evidence of a broader Underdark-induced perceptual breakdown.
source_quote: I took notes. Elin couldn't speak and Daz had a headache and somewhere below us the demon lords were apparently still broadcasting...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, a dwarf with native understanding of Dwarven, noticed the Stroudite inscription on Tarvis Ulain’s monument and later experienced persistent pressure in his head, suggesting he is a secondary recipient of the same Underdark corruption affecting Elin.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir, a Dragonborn, identified the mechanism behind Elin’s condition as non-magical perceptual distortion — the world arriving as an unprocessable language — and contributed critical analysis to the group’s understanding of the phenomenon.
source_quote: Zalthir articulated the mechanism: the input, the audio, the way the world was arriving at her rather than the world itself.

subject: Daggerford Market Square
fact: Daggerford’s market square hosts a bronze monument to Tarvis Ulain, featuring a severed forearm, a Stroudite inscription, and a Gauntlet-approved record, making it a focal point of religious and political tension.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where the party first encountered the priest selling pewter hand casts of Tarvis Ulain’s arm, and where the priest’s reaction to their diverse composition revealed societal unease around inter-factional alliances.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn, named after a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades ago, retains the wall where he died and features a bard performing 'The Kenku Could Not Fly,' which Daz interprets as a metaphor for strategic restraint.
source_quote: A wizard, burned alive, dragon cult, decades prior... That is where he fell... We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: bronze forearm monument
fact: The bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain is a severed, mounted limb with no weapon, bearing a Dwarven Stroudite inscription ('The move is yours') and a Common Gauntlet record, symbolizing the collision of faiths and forgotten histories.
source_quote: A bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar. Not holding anything. Just a hand.

subject: pewter hand casts
fact: Miniature pewter reproductions of Tarvis Ulain’s severed hand are sold as charms by a priest, marketed as donations to the Order of the Gauntlet, and perceived as grotesque souvenirs by the party.
source_quote: Small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast, miniature things, charm-sized.

subject: six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin’s compulsive drawings of a six-pointed star on every flat surface are a non-verbal communication of her perceptual breakdown, possibly representing a corrupted concept of 'wells' or divine access points.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface... a six-pointed star, over and over.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: The presence of a Stroudite chess reference ('The move is yours') on a Bahamutian paladin’s monument in Daggerford suggests a hidden, unacknowledged alliance or ideological overlap between the two faiths, raising theological and political questions.
source_quote: Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin in a town I'd barely heard of...

subject: Underdark perceptual bleed
fact: A non-magical, systemic corruption from the Underdark is affecting surface dwellers’ perception, causing hallucinations, silence, and headaches, implying the demon lords are no longer confined below and are rewriting reality’s language.
source_quote: The madness from the Underdark... was not, apparently, staying below. It was reaching up.

subject: Daz's headache and Elin's silence
fact: Daz’s persistent head pressure and Elin’s inability to speak may be symptoms of the same phenomenon — an external, non-magical corruption that disrupts how the world is received — suggesting a shared, unexplained vulnerability among those attuned to deeper truths.
source_quote: I looked at him. I looked at Elin. I thought about what we'd just established: that something from below was bleeding up...

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford, marking the timeline of the monument’s creation and the beginning of the town’s quiet spiritual reckoning.
source_quote: Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years.

subject: two years after the war
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the Tarvis Ulain monument two years after the war, indicating the delayed, institutional nature of post-conflict memorialization and ideological compromise.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: six days
fact: Elin has been silent for six days, during which she has compulsively drawn the six-pointed star, establishing the duration of her perceptual crisis and the pattern of her non-verbal communication.
source_quote: My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a shadow monk who survived the Underdark through unconventional means, rejecting formal training in favor of what works. He now navigates Candlekeep’s rigid traditions with quiet defiance, recognizing that his deviations are not errors but adaptations.
source_quote: Absolutely," I said. It was. Patience under provocation. Maintaining stillness when the environment is actively hostile. Responding to aggression without being ruled by it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a scholar whose interest in Stroud’s chess game is performed with exaggerated intensity, masking a deeper obsession with patterns of decay and forgotten doctrines. He collects anomalies like relics, noting their cadences and distortions with ritual precision.
source_quote: The only love I remember during the previous campaign," he said, "involved giants, and it wasn't Stroud's.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin processes the world through conversation and observation, often revealing hidden truths by asking the wrong questions. He accepts paradoxes as natural — whether it’s a sentient ooze becoming a monk or the sea being defeated by light — and finds peace in surrender rather than resolution.
source_quote: Life takes you in weird directions and weird places," he said. "You just gotta go with it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a sentient grey ooze, has been shaped by Zalthir’s guidance into an unlikely monk-in-training. He absorbs lessons through conflict, treating the spy’s attempts to kill him as spiritual exercises — his formlessness becoming a metaphor for adaptability.
source_quote: Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?

subject: The Spy (Miniaturized House T'sarran Operative)
fact: The spy is a prisoner who demands incarceration not for safety, but for legitimacy — she wants to be seen as a captive of authority, not a burden carried by adventurers. Her fury stems from being treated as a tool rather than a person.
source_quote: I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a two-hundred-year-old half-elf shadow monk who refused an order decades ago and now serves as a silent archivist of forgotten lineages. He tests others not to judge their skill, but to reveal what they have become through their choices.
source_quote: This question is for you, not for me.

subject: The Blind Monk
fact: The blind monk is an examiner bound by tradition, judging Zalthir by scrolls that no longer apply. His rigid metrics fail to account for survival-based mastery — yet he recognizes Zalthir’s power, even as he cannot name it.
source_quote: You have learned nothing.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is an institution of knowledge that refuses to hold prisoners, preferring exile over incarceration — yet it is also a place where anomalies are cataloged, tested, and sometimes preserved. Its authority lies not in punishment, but in observation and silence.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them.

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: Zalthir underwent a formal test of shadow monk discipline in Candlekeep’s Echoing Hall, where every technique he performed was deemed 'technically wrong' — yet his results outperformed tradition. The trial exposed the failure of institutional assessment to recognize adaptive mastery.
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: The Note: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.'
fact: A cryptic note on Khell-Vire’s desk references Zalthir’s journey and an unknown entity — the Bone King — whose singing may mark an impending event. Neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire can place it, but its presence suggests a hidden lineage or prophecy tied to the Underdark’s collapse.
source_quote: Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.

subject: The Chant of the Field Ward Preacher
fact: A rhythmic, liturgical chant — identical to one previously heard from Eldred (the madman) and the Field Ward Preacher — is being recited by a young scholar in Candlekeep. Its cadence is subtly corrupted, suggesting a spreading pattern of psychic decay or ritual corruption tied to the Underdark’s madness.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong.

subject: The Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall is a corridor in Candlekeep’s north inner ward where sound returns altered — not as echo, but as echo with commentary. It is a place where truth is reflected imperfectly, making it ideal for testing those who operate outside doctrine.
source_quote: Stone corridors... have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Candlekeep's Bell Tower Cells
fact: Candlekeep’s bell tower contains rarely-used cells with localized anti-magic properties — designed not for imprisonment, but for temporary detention. Their existence is a contradiction: a place meant to hold, yet never to keep — reflecting the institution’s philosophy of delay over resolution.
source_quote: Comfortable, localized anti-magic. They are very rarely used.

subject: The Miniaturized House T'sarran Spy
fact: A tiny, sentient spy from House T'sarran, magically reduced and carried in a bag with Glabbagool. She is not merely a tool but a being who demands recognition — her captivity is psychological as much as physical, and her fury stems from being treated as an object.
source_quote: I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: The Shadow Monk Under-Robe
fact: Khell-Vire wears a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath his Candlekeep gray — a silent declaration that identity outlasts institution. It is not a relic, but a living memory, worn like skin.
source_quote: You don't stop dressing like what you were. You just layer something else over it.

subject: The Day of Arrival at Candlekeep
fact: The day Zalthir and his party arrived at Candlekeep marks the convergence of the Underdark’s madness, the spy’s rebellion, and the institution’s refusal to resolve. It is the first day of delay — and perhaps, the beginning of something that cannot be contained.
source_quote: Centuries do that to a building.

subject: The Difference Between Solutions and Postponements
fact: A lesson from Candlekeep’s monastery — remembered only in fragments — suggests that many acts of justice are not resolutions but delays. Zalthir now lives this truth: keeping the spy is not saving her, but postponing her fate.
source_quote: I remember nothing else from that class. I remember wanting to be in the training hall.

subject: Is Wisdom the Same as Resignation?
fact: Thorin’s statement — 'You just gotta go with it' — haunts the party. Is it acceptance? Or surrender? The line blurs in Candlekeep, where knowledge is preserved, but change is deferred — and the only certainty is that some things will never be solved.
source_quote: I have not yet decided whether it is wisdom or resignation. Possibly there is not much difference.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combatant who ignored the manual, built a unique shadow-step-and-hit technique, and now embodies the most interesting aspect of shadow monkery — his combination of movement and strike redeems his lack of traditional skills.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a perceptive shadow master who recognized that Zalthir’s unorthodox technique — born of disregard for the manual — is the true innovation in shadow monkery, and offered him a specialized technique in acknowledgment.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade who endured millennia of darkness and disuse, and is now undergoing a two-stage healing process — first remembering daylight without fighting, then grieving her past wielder — as recognized by Master Archivist Philemon.
source_quote: She needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight. And then, when she's ready, and you are willing, she needs to grieve.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is a master archivist who shifted from viewing Dawnbringer as a specimen to recognizing her as a sentient being with emotional trauma, and adapted his approach to honor her personhood.
source_quote: Your sword — she needs to remember what daylight feels like without needing to fight.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a drow with amnesia who broke cultural norms by offering raw, unfiltered truth to a Candlekeep librarian in exchange for knowledge — rejecting manipulation in favor of vulnerability.
source_quote: I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story... I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Sister Yvenne
fact: Sister Yvenne is a Candlekeep Avowed who enforces reciprocal knowledge exchange with quiet authority, and was visibly unsettled yet convinced by Daz’s unprecedented honesty.
source_quote: Wow, that's quite a bit.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a drow city governed by rigid hierarchy, transactional loyalty, and systemic betrayal — where survival requires erasing entire houses, and failure to do so invites annihilation.
source_quote: If you left a single person alive — even a child, even someone inconvenient and useless — your house was forfeit.

subject: shadow technique award
fact: Zalthir was awarded a specialized shadow technique after demonstrating an unorthodox, manually-ignored method that combined shadow step and strike — a breakthrough acknowledged by Khell-Vire as the most significant aspect of his combat identity.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: Dawnbringer's healing enrollment
fact: Dawnbringer was formally enrolled in a two-stage healing process — light reclamation and mourning — initiated by Philemon after recognizing her sentient trauma from centuries of darkness and disuse.
source_quote: We're all gonna grow out of this. Hopefully, Dawnbringer grows a plus one.

subject: Daz's truth disclosure
fact: Daz disclosed his full, unfiltered history — amnesia, imprisonment, escape from the Underdark — to Sister Yvenne, breaking drow cultural norms and triggering a rare moment of trust in Candlekeep’s knowledge exchange system.
source_quote: I just couldn't afford the usual approach. When you don't know what you're hiding, you can't protect it.

subject: Daz's identity
fact: Daz is a potential survivor of a wiped-out Menzoberranzan house — the 'blithering idiot' — and his amnesia, headache, and drow heritage may be linked to a forbidden legacy the city tried to erase.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Dawnbringer's first wielder
fact: Dawnbringer’s silence upon being asked about her previous wielder suggests deep trauma tied to a death or betrayal — one that may be central to her need to grieve, and which remains unspoken.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind.

subject: The 'blithering idiot' legacy
fact: Menzoberranzan’s doctrine requires total annihilation of rival houses — yet one survivor, a 'blithering idiot,' escaped and may now be Daz — a living anomaly that challenges the city’s control over memory and history.
source_quote: Unclear... Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Shadow Monk Doctrine Failure
fact: The official shadow monk manual is fundamentally wrong about Zalthir — his unorthodox technique, built in spite of it, proves that true mastery arises not from adherence but from innovation — a systemic failure of the tradition.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a library governed by strict reciprocity — information exchanged only when both sides contribute — where scholars like Philemon and Yvenne enforce knowledge ethics with ritual precision.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a drow city where power is maintained through betrayal, surveillance, and the total erasure of enemies — where even a child left alive is considered a fatal flaw.
source_quote: They just don't use words like *reciprocal exchange*. They use knives.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a realm of perpetual darkness where Dawnbringer suffered centuries of disuse, and where Daz was imprisoned, escaped, and began his journey toward self-discovery.
source_quote: We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada.

subject: Resonant Slime
fact: Resonant Slime is a magical vial produced by a xenobiology sage after observing the sentient gelatinous cube’s progress — used to affirm its sentience and potential as a student.
source_quote: Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: Pocket Drow
fact: Pocket Drow is a small, living drow kept by Thorin — a symbolic and possibly sentient companion that represents the unexpected, non-threatening presence of drow culture outside Menzoberranzan’s violent norms.
source_quote: Pocket Drow.

subject: Gelatinous Cube (Glabbagool)
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient gelatinous cube being trained as a monk — capable of walking, torturing drows, and learning shadow techniques — defying the assumption that it is a mindless digestive system.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student. He's learning the ways of the monk. He's already walking.

subject: Eldritch Tattoo (Shadow Tentacles)
fact: The eldritch tattoo on Zalthir manifests shadow tentacles — a learned, unstable, and non-standard ability that emerged from his unorthodox training and is now part of his combat identity.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: Drow (tortured)
fact: A drow, likely a captive or prisoner, is being 'tortured' by Glabbagool — a sign of the cube’s emerging agency, moral ambiguity, and internalization of drow cultural violence as part of its learning.
source_quote: He's already torturing this poor drow.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during a single, continuous narrative arc — likely a single session or multi-hour roleplay sequence — marked by thematic recursion, character breakthroughs, and meta-commentary on lore and system failure.
source_quote: Then: 'You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.'

subject: Shadow Monks
fact: The Shadow Monks are a tradition bound by rigid manuals and doctrines — now revealed as fundamentally flawed, because Zalthir’s innovations, born of ignoring them, represent the true path of the shadow.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a companion who provides blunt, humorous commentary — notably naming the 'Pocket Drow' — and serves as a grounding voice amid surreal and philosophical developments.
source_quote: Pocket Drow.

subject: The Headache
fact: Daz’s persistent headache may be a psychic echo of Menzoberranzan’s erased memories — a haunting residue of the house that was wiped out, and of the identity he was meant to forget.
source_quote: My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: Hall of Divination
fact: The Hall of Divination is a Candlekeep archive saturated with residual spell energy, where knowledge moves autonomously — and where Daz’s raw honesty disrupted the expected drow behavioral script.
source_quote: Spectral mage hands drift between the shelves, fetching tomes for researchers who don't look up.

subject: Clay Tablet
fact: Philemon’s clay tablet was used to record Dawnbringer as a specimen — later abandoned when he recognized her as a sentient being — symbolizing the shift from objectification to personhood.
source_quote: He had a small clay tablet ready. He was already writing... He set the tablet down.

subject: The Way of the Shadow
fact: The Way of the Shadow is not about hitting — it is about discrete movement — and Zalthir’s combination of shadow step and strike, though unorthodox, proves he has internalized its true essence.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas.

subject: Zalthir's final strike
fact: Zalthir performed a final, precise strike through the shadows themselves — landing with unambiguous power — which prompted Khell-Vire to recognize his transformation and offer him a specialized technique.
source_quote: His strike landed at a number that left no ambiguity.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is a master of shadow monkery who recognized that Zalthir’s unorthodox method — though violating the manual — embodies the true philosophy of the shadow: movement over force, combination over conformity.
source_quote: There is something special about how you hit. The way of the Shadow is not about hitting. It is about discrete movement.

subject: The Manual Was Wrong
fact: The official shadow monk manual failed to account for Zalthir’s innovation — proving that the most powerful expressions of the tradition arise not from adherence, but from rebellion and synthesis.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: Yvenne
fact: Yvenne is a custodian of restricted knowledge in Menzoberranzan, maintaining the public record's appearance while withholding truths beyond its scope, her physical stillness betraying deliberate concealment.
source_quote: Yvenne’s body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes.

subject: Houses of Menzoberranzan
fact: Several noble houses in Menzoberranzan historically bore the name Daz'issin — a maternal diminutive for sons meant to ensure survival — but nearly all perished, suggesting systemic erasure tied to the name's usage.
source_quote: The houses that had used it, most of them, did not last.

subject: Striking of the Fourth Seat
fact: The fourth seat in Menzoberranzan’s hierarchy holds ritual archive privileges, allowing legal access to and alteration of records; its being 'struck' was not political deletion but a sophisticated, infrastructural erasure requiring payment, influence, and obfuscation.
source_quote: Having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records. That a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind.

subject: Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe
fact: A two-hundred-year-old heraldic text, deliberately defaced by a razor cut removing an appendix referenced in a footnote, which contained the only known record of Daz'issin’s full lineage and context.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: Daz'issin is a diminutive name meaning 'small shadow,' used by mothers in Menzoberranzan to invoke protection for sons — not a title, not a house, but a whispered plea for survival that became a target for annihilation.
source_quote: Mothers use it for boys they wanted to live. That there were not many uses of it in the past three centuries.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a shortened form of Daz'issin, likely a childhood name given by a mother seeking to protect him in Menzoberranzan — a name that marks him as a survivor of erased lineage and a target of deliberate historical suppression.
source_quote: Well, isn't my name, Daz? Maybe it's my full name?

subject: The Missing Appendix
fact: The appendix referenced in the footnote of the heraldic text was physically excised — a deliberate act of historical sabotage — leaving no record of Daz'issin’s true identity, lineage, or the circumstances of his family’s destruction.
source_quote: The footnote referenced an appendix. The appendix was missing.

subject: The Library Room
fact: The room is a repository of total knowledge by reputation, yet something essential is absent — a curated void indicating that the library’s preservation is a lie, and its true function is selective erasure.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here.

subject: The Silent Patron
fact: The patron who protected Daz is unknown, but their existence is implied by his survival — and their silence is the only record left, suggesting they are either dead, erased, or still active under cover.
source_quote: Let us turn to your patron, she said. Did you not come here to learn who protected you?

subject: Historical Erasure of Daz'issin Lineage
fact: The systematic removal of all records pertaining to Daz'issin — through book mutilation, archive strikes, and house annihilation — constitutes a large-scale, deliberate, and costly act of memory destruction targeting a single name and its bearers.
source_quote: That is not a small act. That is a very large, very expensive, very deliberate act.
